CLI users should keep using the \u003ccode\u003eCOMPOSE_FILE\u003c/code\u003e\noverlay workflow above. For stack UIs, point the stack at one of the standalone\nfiles instead, which bundle the base stack plus the GPU settings:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003edocker-compose.gpu-nvidia.yml\u003c/code\u003e — still requires the NVIDIA Container Toolkit\non the host.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003edocker-compose.gpu-amd.yml\u003c/code\u003e — still requires host ROCm/kfd/DRI setup, the\n\u003ccode\u003evideo\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003erender\u003c/code\u003e group membership, and \u003ccode\u003eRENDER_GID\u003c/code\u003e when needed.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe base \u003ccode\u003edocker-compose.yml\u003c/code\u003e plus the \u003ccode\u003edocker/gpu.*.yml\u003c/code\u003e overlays remain the\nsource of truth; the standalone files mirror them for single-file deployments.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eVerify after enabling either overlay:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"docker compose exec odysseus nvidia-smi -L   # NVIDIA\ndocker compose exec odysseus sh -lc 'test -e /dev/kfd \u0026amp;\u0026amp; test -d /dev/dri \u0026amp;\u0026amp; ls -l /dev/kfd /dev/dri/renderD*'  # AMD\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003edocker compose \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003eexec\u003c/span\u003e odysseus nvidia-smi -L   \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e NVIDIA\u003c/span\u003e\ndocker compose \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003eexec\u003c/span\u003e odysseus sh -lc \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003etest -e /dev/kfd \u0026amp;\u0026amp; test -d /dev/dri \u0026amp;\u0026amp; ls -l /dev/kfd /dev/dri/renderD*\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e  \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e AMD\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGPU passthrough ≠ llama.cpp CUDA.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003envidia-smi\u003c/code\u003e passing inside the\ncontainer confirms Docker GPU access, but llama.cpp also needs \u003ccode\u003ecudart\u003c/code\u003e and\nthe CUDA Toolkit at runtime. If Cookbook logs show \u003ccode\u003eUnable to find cudart library\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eCould NOT find CUDAToolkit\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eCUDA Toolkit not found\u003c/code\u003e, or\ntensors/layers assigned to CPU, that is a Cookbook/llama.cpp build issue —\nnot a Docker passthrough failure. Reinstall the serve engine via\n\u003cstrong\u003eCookbook → Dependencies\u003c/strong\u003e to get a CUDA-enabled build.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe same split applies to AMD/ROCm: seeing \u003ccode\u003e/dev/kfd\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003e/dev/dri\u003c/code\u003e inside\nthe container confirms device passthrough, not ROCm userspace or a\nROCm-enabled vLLM/llama.cpp build. \u003ccode\u003erocm-smi\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003erocminfo\u003c/code\u003e are not expected\ninside the slim Odysseus image.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOllama with Docker.\u003c/strong\u003e If Ollama runs on the host, add this endpoint in\nSettings:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1\"\u003e\u003cpre lang=\"text\" class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ehttp://host.docker.internal:11434/v1\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOllama must listen outside its own loopback interface:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 ollama serve\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003eOLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 ollama serve\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis connects Odysseus in Docker to an Ollama server that is already running on\nyour host machine; it does not start Ollama inside the container.\n\u003ccode\u003ehost.docker.internal\u003c/code\u003e is Docker's hostname for the host machine from inside the\ncontainer. Cookbook \u003cstrong\u003eServe\u003c/strong\u003e is a separate workflow for serving downloaded\nmodels through Odysseus/llama.cpp, so Windows users with an existing Ollama\ninstall usually only need to add the endpoint in Settings.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUseful checks.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"docker compose ps\ndocker compose logs --tail=120 odysseus\ndocker compose logs odysseus | grep -E 'ChromaDB|MemoryVectorStore|DEGRADED'\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003edocker compose ps\ndocker compose logs --tail=120 odysseus\ndocker compose logs odysseus \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e|\u003c/span\u003e grep -E \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003eChromaDB|MemoryVectorStore|DEGRADED\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003emacOS details.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003estart-macos.sh\u003c/code\u003e installs Homebrew deps, creates the venv,\nruns setup, and starts uvicorn on port \u003ccode\u003e7860\u003c/code\u003e because AirPlay often holds\n\u003ccode\u003e7000\u003c/code\u003e. It uses llama.cpp/Ollama for Metal. vLLM/SGLang are CUDA/ROCm-only and\ndo not run on macOS. Treat it like an admin console.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eKeep \u003ccode\u003eAUTH_ENABLED=true\u003c/code\u003e for any network-accessible deployment.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eKeep \u003ccode\u003eLOCALHOST_BYPASS=false\u003c/code\u003e outside local development.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eUse \u003ccode\u003eSECURE_COOKIES=true\u003c/code\u003e when Odysseus is served through HTTPS by a trusted reverse proxy or private access gateway.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eDo not expose it directly to the public internet without HTTPS and a trusted reverse proxy or private access layer.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eKeep \u003ccode\u003e.env\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003edata/\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003elogs/\u003c/code\u003e, databases, uploads, generated media, backups, auth/session files, API keys, and model/provider tokens out of Git and private shares. They are ignored by default.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eReview \u003ccode\u003edata/auth.json\u003c/code\u003e after first boot: disable open signup unless you intentionally want it, make only your own account admin, and keep demo/test accounts non-admin.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eNon-admin users do not get shell/Python/file read/write by default, and admin-only routes/tools such as MCP management, API tokens, webhooks, model/cookbook serving, backup/vault, and app settings are admin-gated. Other features are controlled by per-user privileges, so review each user's privileges before exposing a deployment.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eRotate any API keys or tokens that were ever pasted into a shared chat, demo, screenshot, or log.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eIf you enable API tokens or webhooks, create separate tokens per integration and delete unused ones.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ePrefer binding manual development runs to \u003ccode\u003e127.0.0.1\u003c/code\u003e; bind to \u003ccode\u003e0.0.0.0\u003c/code\u003e only when you intentionally want LAN/reverse-proxy access.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eKeep ChromaDB, SearXNG, ntfy, Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp, databases, and raw model/provider APIs internal-only. Expose only the authenticated Odysseus web/API entrypoint through your trusted proxy or private access layer.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eBefore publishing a fork, run \u003ccode\u003egit status --short\u003c/code\u003e and confirm no private files from \u003ccode\u003e.env\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003edata/\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003elogs/\u003c/code\u003e, uploads, backups, or local databases are staged.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003ePrivate or proxied deployments\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-private-or-proxied-deployments\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Private or proxied deployments\" href=\"#private-or-proxied-deployments\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOdysseus serves plain HTTP on its app port. Docker Compose binds Odysseus and the bundled services to \u003ccode\u003e127.0.0.1\u003c/code\u003e by default, so a typical production/private setup is:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eKeep Odysseus on localhost, for example \u003ccode\u003e127.0.0.1:7000\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eTerminate HTTPS at a trusted reverse proxy or private access gateway.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ePut the authenticated Odysseus web/API entrypoint behind that layer.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eKeep raw service and model ports internal-only.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eCloudflare Access, Tailscale, Caddy, nginx, and Traefik can all fit this pattern; none are required by Odysseus. class="react-directory-row-commit-cell"><div><div class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="ci: security scanning suite and governance (consolidates #305-310) (#1314)

* ci: add security scanning suite and governance

Consolidates the security CI work into one reviewable change. Adds, as
separate workflow files under .github/workflows/:

- secret-scan.yml      gitleaks (pinned + checksum-verified), full history
- workflow-security.yml actionlint + zizmor, audits the workflows themselves
- dependency-review.yml PR dependency gate + advisory pip-audit
- container-scan.yml    hadolint (blocking) + Trivy image scan (advisory)
- codeql.yml            CodeQL for Python and JS, main + weekly

Plus .github/dependabot.yml (pip/npm/actions/docker), .github/CODEOWNERS,
and docs/security-ci.md explaining each check and the one-time settings.

All additive: no existing files are modified. Actions are pinned to commit
SHAs, tokens default-deny (permissions: {}), advisory scans never block,
and SARIF upload is gated to push so fork PRs do not fail on a read-only
token. Composes with the correctness CI in #1015.

* ci(security): isolate Trivy from the Dockerfile lint gate

Address review on #1314 (points 2 and 3).

container-scan.yml now runs only hadolint (the blocking Dockerfile lint)
and keeps the broad pull_request + push:[main] trigger so the required
check always reports and never hangs a PR.

The advisory image scan moves to container-trivy.yml, split by event:
  - pull_request / workflow_dispatch: build and scan under contents:read
    only, no SARIF upload. The image build runs PR-supplied Dockerfile
    instructions, so this path holds no write scope.
  - push to main: build, scan, and upload SARIF with security-events:write.
    Only this trusted path is granted write.
This stops PR jobs from requesting security-events:write they never use,
and a paths-ignore (matching docker-publish.yml) skips the image rebuild
on docs-only changes.

docs/security-ci.md: correct the trigger description to "every pull
request and every push to main", matching the workflows and the existing
ci.yml convention.

Verified locally: zizmor --offline --min-severity=low and actionlint are
clean on the changed and new workflow files.

credentials or a working config.

starting.

suite and governance (consolidates #305-310) (#1314)

* ci: add security scanning suite and governance

Consolidates the security CI work into one reviewable change. Adds, as
separate workflow files under .github/workflows/:

- secret-scan.yml      gitleaks (pinned + checksum-verified), full history
- workflow-security.yml actionlint + zizmor, audits the workflows themselves
- dependency-review.yml PR dependency gate + advisory pip-audit
- container-scan.yml    hadolint (blocking) + Trivy image scan (advisory)
- codeql.yml            CodeQL for Python and JS, main + weekly

Plus .github/dependabot.yml (pip/npm/actions/docker), .github/CODEOWNERS,
and docs/security-ci.md explaining each check and the one-time settings.

All additive: no existing files are modified. Actions are pinned to commit
SHAs, tokens default-deny (permissions: {}), advisory scans never block,
and SARIF upload is gated to push so fork PRs do not fail on a read-only
token. Composes with the correctness CI in #1015.

* ci(security): isolate Trivy from the Dockerfile lint gate

Address review on #1314 (points 2 and 3).

container-scan.yml now runs only hadolint (the blocking Dockerfile lint)
and keeps the broad pull_request + push:[main] trigger so the required
check always reports and never hangs a PR.

The advisory image scan moves to container-trivy.yml, split by event:
  - pull_request / workflow_dispatch: build and scan under contents:read
    only, no SARIF upload. The image build runs PR-supplied Dockerfile
    instructions, so this path holds no write scope.
  - push to main: build, scan, and upload SARIF with security-events:write.
    Only this trusted path is granted write.
This stops PR jobs from requesting security-events:write they never use,
and a paths-ignore (matching docker-publish.yml) skips the image rebuild
on docs-only changes.

docs/security-ci.md: correct the trigger description to "every pull
request and every push to main", matching the workflows and the existing
ci.yml convention.

Verified locally: zizmor --offline --min-severity=low and actionlint are
clean on the changed and new workflow files.

debug loop: persistent log files, auto-adopt orphan tmux, Codex/Claude skill parity

Three converging fixes so the chat agent + external Codex/Claude skills can actually debug a crashed serve instead of staring at a post-crash neofetch banner:

* Serves now `tee` to /tmp/odysseus-tmux/SESSION.log on the host running them. Runner saves fds 3/4 before the tee and restores them right before `exec ${SHELL}`, so the post-crash interactive zsh banner does NOT pollute the log file.
* `tail_serve_output` (chat agent) and `/api/codex/cookbook/output/{sid}` (Codex+Claude skills) both prefer the persistent log file over the tmux pane. Pane is fallback for sessions predating the tee runner. Default tail bumped 150 -> 400.
* `list_served_models` "recent log" snippet seeks to the Traceback line instead of showing the last 6 lines (which was always the bash prompt).

Cookbook auto-adoption sweep on `/api/cookbook/tasks/status`: every 20s (rate-limited) the cookbook SSHes each configured server, finds `serve-*` / `cookbook-*` tmux sessions running an actual model process (vllm/python/llama-server/etc., filtered via `pane_current_command`), and writes them into state.tasks. So when the agent falls back to raw ssh+tmux, the session appears in the Cookbook UI on the next poll.

`serve_model` error path now reads `data["detail"]` in addition to `data["error"]` so the FastAPI HTTPException message ("Invalid characters in cmd") actually reaches the agent instead of being swallowed as a generic "Serve failed". Tool description updated to warn against `cd …`/`source …`/`&&` prefixes.

Intent-without-action supervisor in agent_loop: when the model writes "Let me tail the output" / "I'll check the logs" / "Let me investigate" and ends the turn without emitting a tool call, the loop injects a sharp system nudge ("You said you would X — DO IT NOW") and continues. Capped at 2 nudges per chat so a model that genuinely cannot use the tool does not pin the loop.

Codex/Claude skill parity: adds `/cookbook/cached`, `/cookbook/presets`, `/cookbook/preset/{name}`, `/cookbook/adopt` so external agents have the same surface as the chat agent. SKILL.md docs + odysseus_api.py wrapper updated for both bundles.

`adopt_served_model` promoted to the always-on tool set so the agent has a documented fallback when serve_model rejects a cmd.

Also various cookbook UI tweaks accumulated alongside the above (cookbook.js, cookbookRunning.js, cookbookServe.js, cookbook-diagnosis.js, settings.js, style.css)." class="Link--secondary" * Improve Docker GPU setup diagnostics

Add a Docker GPU preflight script for NVIDIA users. The script is
read-only by default, checks host NVIDIA drivers, Docker availability,
and container GPU passthrough, and prints actionable next steps.

Add explicit opt-in modes to print install commands, install NVIDIA
Container Toolkit on Ubuntu/Debian, and enable the NVIDIA Compose overlay
in .env after passthrough is verified.

Document common NVIDIA Docker failure modes, ignore generated .env

class="react-directory-row-commit-cell"><div><div class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="feat(agent): confine agent file/shell tools to a selectable workspace (#3665)

* feat(agent): workspace confinement via context-local binding + get_workspace tool

Bind the per-turn workspace once in execute_tool_block; the shared path
resolvers (_resolve_tool_path / _resolve_search_root) and the subprocess cwd
helper (agent_cwd) read it, so file tools + bash/python are confined centrally
and a new tool that uses the shared helpers cannot accidentally bypass it.

Adds the admin-gated /api/workspace/browse picker, a workspace pill + directory
modal (reusing existing modal/button CSS), the /workspace slash command, and a
get_workspace tool (replaces a system-prompt block). Confinement is OS-agnostic
(realpath/normcase/commonpath) and docker-safe (container paths, no host
assumptions). Reopens #2023.

* ux(workspace): clarify workspace is not a sandbox

Picker modal note + pill tooltip + get_workspace tool/output wording now state
plainly: read_file/write_file/edit_file/grep/glob/ls are confined to the folder,
but bash/python only start there (cwd) and are not sandboxed. Modal note reuses
the existing .muted class.

* fix(agent): treat an active workspace as file-work intent

A vague low-signal message (e.g. "look at the local project") matches no
domain keywords, so tool retrieval is skipped and only always-available tools
are offered — leaving the agent with no file access even though a workspace is
set. When a workspace is active, include the file/code tools (incl.
get_workspace) on low-signal turns so the agent can act on the folder.

Also requires the tool index (ChromaDB) to be reachable for normal retrieval;
that is an environment dependency, not part of this change.

* ux(workspace): hide pill + overflow entry in chat mode

Workspace only scopes the agent's file/shell tools, so the pill and the
overflow 'Workspace' entry are agent-only now — hidden in chat mode like the
bash toggle. Mode read from the DOM in syncWorkspaceIndicator; applyMode() is
called from the agent/chat setMode handler.

* prompt(tools): steer bash/python to defer to the dedicated file tools

bash/python schema descriptions (what native-tool-calling models read) were
bare and gave no steer, so models would do file ops via the shell (e.g. writing
SVG/HTML, which then dumps raw markup into the tool preview). Tell bash/python
in the schema + tool-index + prompt section to prefer read_file/write_file/
edit_file/grep/glob/ls and only be used for what those do not cover.

* prompt(tools): keep bash/python deferral generic (no hardcoded tool names)

Reference 'a dedicated tool' rather than listing read_file/write_file/grep/etc.
by name, so the guidance does not go stale if those tools are renamed.

* style(workspace): drop em-dashes from added code comments/strings

* ux(workspace): terser non-sandbox note in picker (no tool-name list)

* ux(workspace): mirror terse non-sandbox wording in pill tooltip

* chore: untrack local venv symlink (run-only, not part of the feature)

* prompt(workspace): keep get_workspace text generic (no hardcoded tool names)

* fix(agent): low-signal + workspace surfaces only read-only file tools

Intersect the files tool group with PLAN_MODE_READONLY_TOOLS so a vague message
in a workspace exposes read_file/grep/glob/ls/get_workspace for exploration, but
not write_file/edit_file/bash/python -- those wait for a request that actually
calls for them (RAG retrieval still adds them on a real ask).

* feat(workspace): cap browse listing at 500 dirs with a truncated hint

Mirror the filesystem_tools._CODENAV_MAX_HITS pattern with a module-local
_MAX_BROWSE_DIRS so a directory with thousands of children does not dump every
row into the picker; the response carries a truncated flag and the modal tells
the user to type a path to jump in.

* chore: untrack local venv symlink (run-only artifact)

* fix(workspace): vet the workspace root against the sensitive-path deny list at bind time

The in-workspace resolver deny-lists sensitive paths inside the workspace,
but the empty-path search root is the workspace itself, so a workspace of
~/.ssh could be listed via ls with no path. vet_workspace() (public, in
tool_execution next to the resolvers) rejects non-directories and sensitive
roots before the path is ever bound; chat_routes uses it instead of its
inline isdir check.

* fix(workspace): reject filesystem roots and stop showing rejected workspaces as active

Review findings from #3665:

P2: vet_workspace accepted / (and would accept drive/UNC roots), which makes
every absolute path 'inside' the workspace and collapses confinement into
host-wide file access. A root is its own dirname, so reject when
dirname(resolved) == resolved; the browse response now carries a selectable
flag and the picker disables 'Use this folder' on unselectable dirs.

P3: /workspace set stored any string client-side and the chat route silently
dropped rejected values, so the pill could claim a confinement that was not
in effect. New admin-gated /api/workspace/vet validates manual paths before
they persist (canonical path returned), and when a posted workspace is
rejected at send time the stream emits workspace_rejected so the client
clears the stored value and toasts instead of continuing silently.

* fix(workspace): check caller privilege before vetting the posted workspace

Review finding: /api/chat_stream called vet_workspace() on the posted value
for every caller and emitted workspace_rejected on failure, so a non-admin
who can chat but cannot use file/shell tools could distinguish existing
directories from missing/file/sensitive/root paths by whether the event
appeared. The resolution now lives in _resolve_request_workspace, which
drops the submitted value uniformly for non-admin callers, with no vetting
and no event, before the path ever touches the filesystem. Admin and
single-user behavior is unchanged. Test pins that valid and invalid paths
are indistinguishable for a non-admin and that vet_workspace is never
invoked for them." class="Link--secondary" href="/pewdiepie-archdaemon/odysseus/commit/620fdd0859e3097e45c3ed4cec1b4ffbad05f962">feat(agent): confine agent file/shell tools to a selectable workspace start ChromaDB in start-macos.sh so tool calling works (#3664)

* fix(macos): start ChromaDB from start-macos.sh so tool calling works

start-macos.sh never started ChromaDB, so the tool index failed to initialize
and tool/MCP injection silently degraded on native macOS installs (no Docker).
Start a local chroma from the venv before launching, mirroring the existing
Apfel background+trap pattern: idempotent (skips if 8100 is already serving),
honors CHROMADB_HOST/CHROMADB_PORT (skips when remote), logs to a file, persists
to data/chroma, and is killed in the exit trap.

Fixes #3297

* fix(macos): bind/probe ChromaDB on IPv4 loopback to match app resolution

Binding to the literal localhost can land on IPv6 ::1 while the app connects to
localhost->127.0.0.1, leaving them unable to reach each other. Pin bind + probe
to 127.0.0.1 (0.0.0.0 still honored).

<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/pewdiepie-archdaemon/odysseus/blob/dev/docs/odysseus.jpg"><img src="/pewdiepie-archdaemon/odysseus/raw/dev/docs/odysseus.jpg" alt="Odysseus" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto">A self-hosted AI workspace -- meant to be the self-hosted version of the UI experience you get from ChatGPT and Claude. But with more jank and fun. Running on your own hardware, with your own data -- local-first, privacy-first, and no trojan.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Features</h2><a id="user-content-features" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Features" href="#features"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Chat</strong> -- chat with any local model or API; adding them is super simple.<br>　<sub>vLLM · llama.cpp · Ollama · OpenRouter · OpenAI · GitHub Copilot</sub></li>
<li><strong>Agent</strong> -- hand it tools and let it run the whole task itself.<br>　<sub>built on <a href="https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode">opencode</a> · MCP · web · files · shell · skills · memory</sub></li>
<li><strong>Cookbook</strong> -- Scans your hardware, recommends models, click to download and serve.. easy!<br>　<sub>built on <a href="https://github.com/AlexsJones/llmfit">llmfit</a> · VRAM-aware · GGUF / FP8 / AWQ · fit scoring · vLLM / llama.cpp serving</sub></li>
<li><strong>Deep Research</strong> -- multi-step runs that gather, read, and synthesize sources into a nice visual report.<br>　<sub>adapted from <a href="https://github.com/Alibaba-NLP/DeepResearch">Tongyi DeepResearch</a></sub></li>
<li><strong>Compare</strong> -- a fun tool to compare models side by side. Test completely blind, no bias!<br>　<sub>multi-model · blind test · synthesis</sub></li>
<li><strong>Documents</strong> -- YOU write the text, AI is there to assist, not the opposite.<br>　<sub>multi-tab editor · markdown · HTML · CSV · syntax highlighting · AI edits · suggestions</sub></li>
<li><strong>Memory / Skills</strong> -- Persistent memory and skills, your agent evolves over time as it better understands you and your tasks!<br>　<sub>ChromaDB · fastembed (ONNX) · vector + keyword retrieval · import/export</sub></li>
<li><strong>Email</strong> -- IMAP/SMTP inbox with AI triage built in: urgency reminders, auto-tag, auto-summary, auto-reply drafts, auto-spam.<br>　<sub>IMAP · SMTP · per-account routing · CalDAV-aware</sub></li>
<li><strong>Notes & Tasks</strong> -- Quick notes with reminders, a todo list, and scheduled tasks the agent can act on.<br>　<sub>note pings · checklist · cron-style tasks · ntfy / browser / email channels</sub></li>
<li><strong>Calendar</strong> -- Local-first calendar with CalDAV sync to Radicale / Nextcloud / Apple / Fastmail.<br>　<sub>CalDAV pull · .ics import/export · per-calendar colors · agent-aware</sub></li>
<li><strong>Works on mobile</strong> -- looks and runs great on your phone, not just desktop.<br>　<sub>responsive · installable (PWA) · touch gestures</sub></li>
<li><strong>Extras</strong> -- more to explore, happy if you give it a go!<br>　<sub>image editor · theme editor · file uploads (vision + PDF) · web search · presets · sessions · 2FA</sub></li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Quick Start</h2><a id="user-content-quick-start" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Quick Start" href="#quick-start"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Defaults work out of the box: clone, run, then configure models/search/email
inside <strong>Settings</strong>. Only edit <code>.env</code> for deployment-level overrides like
<code>APP_BIND</code>, <code>APP_PORT</code>, <code>AUTH_ENABLED</code>, <code>DATABASE_URL</code>, or a pre-seeded admin password.</p>
<p dir="auto">On first setup, Odysseus creates an admin account (<code>admin</code> unless
<code>ODYSSEUS_ADMIN_USER</code> is set) and prints a temporary password in the terminal.
For Docker installs, the same line is in <code>docker compose logs odysseus</code>.
Use that for the first login, then change it in <strong>Settings</strong>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Contributing? See <a href="/pewdiepie-archdaemon/odysseus/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md">CONTRIBUTING.md</a> for setup, testing, and
pull request guidelines.</p>

<p dir="auto">To include optional extras in the image (PDF viewer, Office extraction; includes AGPL PyMuPDF), build with <code>docker compose build --build-arg INSTALL_OPTIONAL=true</code> before <code>up</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Open <code>http://localhost:7000</code> when the containers are healthy. Docker Compose
binds the web UI to <code>127.0.0.1</code> by default. If the port is taken, set
<code>APP_PORT=7001</code> in <code>.env</code> and recreate the container. Set <code>APP_BIND=0.0.0.0</code>
only when you intentionally want LAN/reverse-proxy access.</p>

<p dir="auto">Requirements: Python 3.11+. Cookbook also needs <code>tmux</code> for background model

<summary>Cookbook, GPU, Ollama, and troubleshooting notes</summary>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Docker bundled services.</strong> Compose starts Odysseus, ChromaDB, SearXNG, and
ntfy. Odysseus and the bundled service ports bind to <code>127.0.0.1</code> by default, so
they are reachable from the host but not exposed to your LAN/public internet
unless you opt in.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Cookbook storage in Docker.</strong> Downloads live in <code>./data/huggingface</code>
(<code>~/.cache/huggingface</code> in the container). Cookbook-installed Python CLIs and
serve engines live in <code>./data/local</code> (<code>~/.local</code> in the container), so they
survive container recreation.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Remote servers.</strong> In <strong>Cookbook -> Settings -> Servers</strong>, generate the
Odysseus SSH key and add the public key to the remote server's
<code>~/.ssh/authorized_keys</code>. From the host you can also run:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre>ssh-copy-id -i data/ssh/id_ed25519.pub user@server</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

<p dir="auto"><strong>Docker GPU overlays.</strong> CPU-only users can skip this section. Cookbook can
only detect GPUs that Docker exposes to the container — if the host runtime or
device passthrough is not configured, Cookbook sees the iGPU, another card, or
CPU instead of your intended GPU.</p>
<p dir="auto">For NVIDIA, <code>scripts/check-docker-gpu.sh</code> diagnoses GPU passthrough and can
optionally install the host runtime or update <code>.env</code>.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Read-only diagnostic (default — installs nothing, never edits .env):</span>

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Print OS-specific install commands without running them:</span>
scripts/check-docker-gpu.sh --print-install-commands

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Install NVIDIA Container Toolkit on Ubuntu/Debian (requires sudo):</span>

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Write COMPOSE_FILE to .env (only when GPU passthrough is confirmed working):</span>

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Full assisted setup — install toolkit, then enable overlay if passthrough works:</span>

<p dir="auto">Safety notes:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>The app never installs host GPU runtime automatically.</li>
<li>The app never edits <code>.env</code> automatically.</li>
<li><code>.env</code> is only modified when <code>--enable-nvidia-overlay</code> is explicitly passed,
and only after GPU passthrough succeeds. <code>--yes</code> skips prompts but does not
bypass the passthrough gate.</li>
<li><code>.env.bak.*</code> backups created by <code>--enable-nvidia-overlay</code> are ignored by
Git and the Docker build context.</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">For NVIDIA/AMD GPU support, also read the comments in the selected overlay file: docker/gpu.nvidia.yml or docker/gpu.amd.yml.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Stack-management UIs (Portainer, Coolify, Dockhand, etc.).</strong> These tools
often accept only a single Compose file and do not reliably honor <code>COMPOSE_FILE</code>
or multiple <code>-f</code> overlays. CLI users should keep using the <code>COMPOSE_FILE</code>
overlay workflow above. For stack UIs, point the stack at one of the standalone
files instead, which bundle the base stack plus the GPU settings:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>docker-compose.gpu-nvidia.yml</code> — still requires the NVIDIA Container Toolkit
on the host.</li>
<li><code>docker-compose.gpu-amd.yml</code> — still requires host ROCm/kfd/DRI setup, the
<code>video</code>/<code>render</code> group membership, and <code>RENDER_GID</code> when needed.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">The base <code>docker-compose.yml</code> plus the <code>docker/gpu.*.yml</code> overlays remain the
source of truth; the standalone files mirror them for single-file deployments.</p>

<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>GPU passthrough ≠ llama.cpp CUDA.</strong> <code>nvidia-smi</code> passing inside the
container confirms Docker GPU access, but llama.cpp also needs <code>cudart</code> and
the CUDA Toolkit at runtime. If Cookbook logs show <code>Unable to find cudart library</code>, <code>Could NOT find CUDAToolkit</code>, <code>CUDA Toolkit not found</code>, or
tensors/layers assigned to CPU, that is a Cookbook/llama.cpp build issue —
not a Docker passthrough failure. Reinstall the serve engine via
<strong>Cookbook → Dependencies</strong> to get a CUDA-enabled build.</p>
<p dir="auto">The same split applies to AMD/ROCm: seeing <code>/dev/kfd</code> and <code>/dev/dri</code> inside
the container confirms device passthrough, not ROCm userspace or a
ROCm-enabled vLLM/llama.cpp build. <code>rocm-smi</code> and <code>rocminfo</code> are not expected
inside the slim Odysseus image.</p>
</blockquote>

<p dir="auto">This connects Odysseus in Docker to an Ollama server that is already running on
your host machine; it does not start Ollama inside the container.

install usually only need to add the endpoint in Settings.</p>

<p dir="auto"><strong>Requirements:</strong> Python 3.11+. The core app (chat, agent, memory, documents,
email, calendar, deep research) runs fully native. For full <strong>Cookbook</strong> background
model downloads and the agent shell tool, also install
<a href="https://git-scm.com/download/win" rel="nofollow">Git for Windows</a> (provides <code>bash.exe</code>).
Local GPU <em>serving</em> of vLLM/SGLang needs Linux/WSL2; for a local model on Windows,
<a href="https://ollama.com/download" rel="nofollow">Ollama</a> is the easiest path — point Odysseus at
<code>http://localhost:11434/v1</code> in Settings.</p>
<p dir="auto">Open <code>http://localhost:7000</code>, log in with the generated admin password,
and configure everything else inside <strong>Settings</strong>.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Outlook / Office 365 email</h3><a id="user-content-outlook--office-365-email" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Outlook / Office 365 email" href="#outlook--office-365-email"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Odysseus email accounts currently use IMAP/SMTP username-password auth. Outlook
and Microsoft 365 generally require OAuth instead, so normal Microsoft mailbox
passwords will fail. See <a href="/pewdiepie-archdaemon/odysseus/blob/dev/docs/email-outlook.md">docs/email-outlook.md</a> for the
current limitation and the planned integration direction.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Security Notes</h2><a id="user-content-security-notes" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Security Notes" href="#security-notes"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Odysseus is a self-hosted workspace with powerful local tools: shell access, file uploads, model downloads, web research, email/calendar integrations, and API tokens. Treat it like an admin console.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Keep <code>AUTH_ENABLED=true</code> for any network-accessible deployment.</li>
<li>Keep <code>LOCALHOST_BYPASS=false</code> outside local development.</li>
<li>Use <code>SECURE_COOKIES=true</code> when Odysseus is served through HTTPS by a trusted reverse proxy or private access gateway.</li>
<li>Do not expose it directly to the public internet without HTTPS and a trusted reverse proxy or private access layer.</li>
<li>Keep <code>.env</code>, <code>data/</code>, <code>logs/</code>, databases, uploads, generated media, backups, auth/session files, API keys, and model/provider tokens out of Git and private shares. They are ignored by default.</li>
<li>Review <code>data/auth.json</code> after first boot: disable open signup unless you intentionally want it, make only your own account admin, and keep demo/test accounts non-admin.</li>
<li>Non-admin users do not get shell/Python/file read/write by default, and admin-only routes/tools such as MCP management, API tokens, webhooks, model/cookbook serving, backup/vault, and app settings are admin-gated. Other features are controlled by per-user privileges, so review each user's privileges before exposing a deployment.</li>
<li>Rotate any API keys or tokens that were ever pasted into a shared chat, demo, screenshot, or log.</li>
<li>If you enable API tokens or webhooks, create separate tokens per integration and delete unused ones.</li>
<li>Prefer binding manual development runs to <code>127.0.0.1</code>; bind to <code>0.0.0.0</code> only when you intentionally want LAN/reverse-proxy access.</li>
<li>Keep ChromaDB, SearXNG, ntfy, Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp, databases, and raw model/provider APIs internal-only. Expose only the authenticated Odysseus web/API entrypoint through your trusted proxy or private access layer.</li>
<li>Before publishing a fork, run <code>git status --short</code> and confirm no private files from <code>.env</code>, <code>data/</code>, <code>logs/</code>, uploads, backups, or local databases are staged.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Private or proxied deployments</h3><a id="user-content-private-or-proxied-deployments" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Private or proxied deployments" href="#private-or-proxied-deployments"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Odysseus serves plain HTTP on its app port. Docker Compose binds Odysseus and the bundled services to <code>127.0.0.1</code> by default, so a typical production/private setup is:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Keep Odysseus on localhost, for example <code>127.0.0.1:7000</code>.</li>
<li>Terminate HTTPS at a trusted reverse proxy or private access gateway.</li>
<li>Put the authenticated Odysseus web/API entrypoint behind that layer.</li>
<li>Keep raw service and model ports internal-only.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Cloudflare Access, Tailscale, Caddy, nginx, and Traefik can all fit this pattern; none are required by Odysseus. If your access layer reaches Odysseus on the same host, proxy to <code>http://127.0.0.1:7000</code> and keep <code>AUTH_ENABLED=true</code>, <code>LOCALHOST_BYPASS=false</code>, and <code>SECURE_COOKIES=true</code>.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Configuration</h2><a id="user-content-configuration" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Configuration" href="#configuration"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Most setup is done inside the app with <code>/setup</code> or <strong>Settings</strong>. Use <code>.env</code>
for deployment-level defaults and secrets you want present before first boot.
Key settings:</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Built-in MCP servers (optional setup)</h3><a id="user-content-built-in-mcp-servers-optional-setup" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Built-in MCP servers (optional setup)" href="#built-in-mcp-servers-optional-setup"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Odysseus auto-registers a few built-in MCP servers at startup. The npx-based ones (currently the browser server, <code>@playwright/mcp</code>) only start when their npm package is already in the local npx cache. If a package isn't cached, that server is skipped with a startup log message explaining what to do, so a fresh install does not block on a multi-minute npm download or hang if Playwright system deps are missing.</p>
<p dir="auto">To enable the browser MCP (page navigation, screenshots, vision), run once:</p>
